subject: Renewal — Dedicated GPU Expansion & Token-Rate SLO Annex (Stellaris)
messages:
From: Laila Ahmed <laila@stellaris.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ops-procurement@stellaris.ai
Date: 2027-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal discussion — projected pool top-up and throughput commitments

Irene / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the Q2 pilot support — the model improvements have knocked our latency out of the park. As we look to finalize renewal, procurement wants a short addendum capturing the additional reserved capacity we discussed and a clear SLO/credit approach tied to tokens/sec guarantees. Key asks from my side:

- Add 4x A100-equivalent GPUs to our reserved pool starting 2027-09-01 (net +4 GPUs).
- Baseline tokens/sec guarantee on the reserved pool: 18,000 tokens/sec sustained, 27,000 tokens/sec burst for 5-minute windows.
- Clear remediation: service credits or dedicated burst credits if sustained throughput drops below baseline for >15 continuous minutes.
- A fallback routing policy to compatible quantified model variants (quantized 8-bit) during capacity pressure, with no more than 10% quality regression on our evaluation set.

Can you provide a short annex we can attach to the renewal that lists these guarantees, the measurement window, monitoring hooks (traces/latency percentiles), and the credit formula? Procurement would like to avoid ambiguous language around "best effort".

Attached is our internal capacity plan (high level) and we can share our eval set if helpful. Happy to jump on a 30-min call to align on precise language.

Thanks,
Laila Ahmed
Head of Platform Ops, Stellaris AI
---
Attachment: stellaris_capacity_plan.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laila Ahmed <laila@stellaris.ai>, ops-procurement@stellaris.ai
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — projected pool top-up and throughput commitments

Hi Laila — thanks for the clear asks. We can absolutely codify a tokens/sec annex; below is a proposed high-level summary for procurement to review. Once you confirm, we'll draft formal language for the renewal addendum and loop in legal.

Proposed summary (for annex):
- Reserved Pool Top-Up: +4 A100-equivalent GPUs starting 2027-09-01 (renewal term start).
- Nominal Throughput Guarantee: 18,000 tokens/sec measured as a 10-minute rolling average across the reserved pool.
- Burst Capacity: 27,000 tokens/sec permitted as a 5-minute rolling peak; bursts are not chargeable beyond committed capacity for the first 12 months of the renewal.
- SLO & Remediation: If the 10-minute rolling average falls below 95% of nominal (i.e., <17,100 tokens/sec) for more than 15 consecutive minutes, customer is eligible for either (a) service credits proportional to the shortfall minutes or (b) one-time burst credit equal to X compute-hours (we will provide the formula in the annex).
- Measurement & Telemetry: Metrics exposed via the Console (per-route tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency) and a shared webhook for alerts.
- Fallback Policy: Automatic routing to a certified 8-bit quantized variant with documented eval-set delta; Redwood will roll back routing if evaluated quality drop exceeds 10% on Stellaris' provided eval set.

I'll assign Marcus to draft the legal-ready annex with the exact credit math and monitoring endpoints.

If that aligns with procurement's expectations, Marcus and I will produce the PDF for DocuSign by Friday.

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laila Ahmed <laila@stellaris.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-02T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — projected pool top-up and throughput commitments

Laila — good to see specifics. A few clarifications we should lock into the annex language:

1) Measurement window & aggregation: we'll state the nominal tokens/sec as a 10-minute rolling average across the entire reserved pool for the customer namespace. Credits will only trigger on pool-level deficits (not per-instance).
2) Latency SLO coupling: credits triggered by throughput shortfall will require that p95 latency for requests routed to the pool is >1.2x the baseline p95 for >15 minutes. This avoids credits for brief backend variances that do not impact request experience.
3) Credit formula (draft): Credit = (Committed_GH * shortfall_ratio * minutes_affected) * $0.85 where Committed_GH is a normalized GPU-hour equivalent for the committed capacity. We'll translate to token-rate terms in the annex.
4) Quality fallback: Redwood will provide a bench report for the quantized variant showing average perplexity delta and our eval harness will run Stellaris' supplied prompts. We recommend a canary for 2 hours before full routing.

I'll prepare a legal-ready SLO Annex (v1.0) with the exact math and monitoring endpoints. Irene — can you confirm whether procurement prefers credits applied to invoice vs. additional burst hours on the account?

—Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: ops-procurement@stellaris.ai
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laila Ahmed <laila@stellaris.ai>, Marcus Reed <m.reed@stellaris.ai>
Date: 2027-08-02T12:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — projected pool top-up and throughput commitments

Hi Marcus / Irene,

Procurement prefers credits applied to the invoice (we have accounting workflows that make burst credits difficult to reconcile). Two additional asks: 1) Can remediations be prorated by minute (preferred) rather than by day? 2) We need explicit SLI definitions in the annex (what counts as a token, how tokens/sec is measured when requests are batched/streamed).

If you can include those two items in the annex (minute-level proration and SLI definitions), we should be able to move quickly. Also, please push the DocuSign link to this thread when ready.

Thanks,
Stellaris Procurement Team

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Draft SLO Annex (v1.0) attached — feedback requested

Team — attaching SLO Annex v1.0 and a pricing workbook with the committed + top-up numbers. Highlights included in the PDF:

- Definitions: token = Unicode codepoint-based tokenization per the attached tokenization spec; for streaming responses tokens/sec is measured at the service ingress aggregated per second before batching aggregation. Batches are de-duplicated for measurement; partial-stream tokens are counted when emitted.
- Measurement granularity: 1-second samples aggregated to 10-minute rolling windows for SLO evaluation.
- Remediation: prorated to the minute. Credits apply to the next invoice.
- Credit math: example scenarios with conversion from tokens/sec shortfall to normalized GPU-hours.
- Canary: 2-hour canary with automatic rollback if quality delta >10% on Stellaris' eval set.

Action items:
- Laila / procurement: confirm acceptance of invoice-applied credits and minute prorating.
- Karthik: I'll need the exact webhook URL and the metric namespace you want exposed for Stellaris.

Link to draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-stellaris-renewal
DocuSign will be prepared once procurement signs off.

—Marcus
